title: Normalized sectionwise universe transport for the published completed-pullback comparison
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a scheme morphism $g:X\to Y$, at independent coefficient and scheme universes. Use the actual completed module categories, ordinary pullback and its adjunction unit from [def-a1-integral-completed-tower-pullback-universes], finite module pullback and its unit from [def-pur-integral-finite-pullback], and the fixed published completed-pullback maps from [def-a1-integral-completed-pullback-interfaces]. For comparison with the fixed published interfaces [def-a1-integral-completed-pullback-interfaces], write $D_{W,n}$ for ordinary scalar extension to $S_{W,n}$ followed by restriction along $\pi_{W,n}$, and $B_{g,n}$ for finite pullback of that reduction followed by restriction. The quotient-unit normalization for an isomorphism $G\circ D_{Y,n}\simeq B_{g,n}$ fixes the pulled unit generator, including every outer scalar. A section transport between module sheaves at possibly different universes is an additive equivalence on every section, commuting with every restriction and semilinear for the specified coefficient ring equivalences. A published coefficient transport consists of completed and finite sectionwise ring equivalences, natural on the small site and compatible with every projection and completed structural map; they factor through the published completedRingIso and finiteRingIso, followed by the integral coefficient universe equivalences. For a published coefficient field $F$ at scheme universe and a section transport of $M_0$ to $M$, an ordinary source/target transport is a pair of such section equivalences on the actual published ordinary source and finite target. The source equivalence sends the published pullback of the quotient unit, with arbitrary outer scalar and restriction to any target site object, to the corresponding ordinary pullback generator. The target equivalence sends every published completedReductionFiniteGenerator to its integral finite pullback tensor, using the finite coefficient equivalences on both scalars. PublishedCompatibility of $e$ means that for every such coefficient and input transport there is a unique normalized source/target transport $tr$ and, on every section, $tr_{target}\circ completedReductionOrdinaryComparison=e\circ tr_{source}$. These are definitions of transport data and normalization predicates, with no existence theorem or chosen comparison.
